raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Fixes #64517

## Problem

The `muse`, `minicpm5` and `poolside_v1` tool parsers keep a parameter's raw text only when its schema is exactly `{"type": "string"}`. For any other string schema they decode the text as JSON (MiniCPM5 and Poolside V1 also fall back to `ast.literal_eval`). A `str | None` parameter (pydantic `Optional[str]`) then gets `"1.10"` as `1.1`, `"1984"` as `1984`, and a JSON file body as an object.

The root cause is a single check `schema.get("type") == "string"` that misses the nullable-string spellings JSON Schema produces for `Optional[str]`:

- `{"anyOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "null"}]}`
- `{"oneOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "null"}]}`
- `{"type": ["string", "null"]}`

## Fix

Add a shared `is_string_schema()` helper in `vllm/tool_parsers/utils.py` that resolves `anyOf`, `oneOf`, and array-type spellings recursively. Use it in all three parsers:

- `muse_tool_parser.py` `_collect_string_params`
- `poolside_v1_tool_parser.py` `_is_string_type`
- `minicpm5xml_tool_parser.py` `_coerce_argument_value`

## Testing

```
tests/tool_parsers/test_utils.py::TestIsStringSchema  7 passed
tests/tool_parsers/test_poolside_v1_tool_parser.py    14 passed
tests/tool_parsers/test_minicpm5xml_tool_parser.py    36 passed
tests/tool_use/test_muse.py -k "string or param"      45 passed
tests/tool_parsers/  728 passed, 1 skipped, 30 xfailed (1 pre-existing error)
```

The pre-existing error is `test_step3p5_tool_parser.py::test_extract_tool_calls_no_tools` failing on `Step3p7TextConfig` import, unrelated to this change.

nodes.body:
Superseded by #64518. Closing rather than keeping a duplicate.

Thanks @smiyamoto3 for running both and calling out the difference. I confirmed your read against #64518's diff: it resolves the string-schema admission for `enum`/`const`, local `$ref`, and `additionalProperties` as well, and it maps `Optional[str]` (`anyOf: [string, null]`) back to `None` when the model emits `null`, where this PR was returning the literal `"null"` string in all three parsers. #64518 is also authored by the issue reporter and landed the broader fix first.

This PR was a narrower subset of that work and carried the `null`-string regression, so there is no independent change left worth landing here. Dropping it in favor of #64518.

(You were also right that the branch had picked up the #61547 scheduler and model-runner commits; that is moot once this is closed.)

I reviewed the fix rather than treating this as a mechanical dedupe: #64518 keeps the raw model text for a string-typed parameter under those schema forms, resolves the admitted type across `$ref` unions, and has the `test_glimmer_keeps_decoding_optional_string` coverage for the optional-string case. Authored with AI assistance.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Thanks for working on this. I noticed #64518 fixes the same issue and was opened a little earlier by the issue author.

I ran both, and the difference I'd look at first is an `Optional[str]` parameter where the model writes `null`: this PR returns the string `"null"` in all three parsers, while main and #64518 return `None`. #64518 covers `enum`, `$ref` and `additionalProperties` string schemas too.

The branch seems to include the #61547 commits as well (scheduler, model runner), so you may want to drop those.

Fixes #64517

## Problem

The `muse`, `minicpm5` and `poolside_v1` tool parsers keep a parameter's raw text only when its schema is exactly `{"type": "string"}`. For any other string schema they decode the text as JSON (MiniCPM5 and Poolside V1 also fall back to `ast.literal_eval`). A `str | None` parameter (pydantic `Optional[str]`) then gets `"1.10"` as `1.1`, `"1984"` as `1984`, and a JSON file body as an object.

The root cause is a single check `schema.get("type") == "string"` that misses the nullable-string spellings JSON Schema produces for `Optional[str]`:

- `{"anyOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "null"}]}`
- `{"oneOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "null"}]}`
- `{"type": ["string", "null"]}`

## Fix

Add a shared `is_string_schema()` helper in `vllm/tool_parsers/utils.py` that resolves `anyOf`, `oneOf`, and array-type spellings recursively. Use it in all three parsers:

- `muse_tool_parser.py` `_collect_string_params`
- `poolside_v1_tool_parser.py` `_is_string_type`

+def _prompt_logprob_rows(
+    prompt_token_ids: GenericSequence[int],
+    prompt_logprobs: GenericSequence[dict[int, Logprob] | None] | None,

+    """Return prompt logprob rows aligned one-to-one with ``prompt_token_ids``.

+    A request resumed after ``reset_prefix_cache`` can keep its prompt token ids
+    while the prompt logprobs that came with the dropped prefill output are gone

+    rows keep their own values.

+    rows: list[dict[int, Logprob] | None] = list(prompt_logprobs or [])
+    if len(rows) < len(prompt_token_ids):
+        rows.extend([None] * (len(prompt_token_ids) - len(rows)))
+    return rows

issue_comments.body:
Superseded by #64518. Closing rather than keeping a duplicate.

Thanks @smiyamoto3 for running both and calling out the difference. I confirmed your read against #64518's diff: it resolves the string-schema admission for `enum`/`const`, local `$ref`, and `additionalProperties` as well, and it maps `Optional[str]` (`anyOf: [string, null]`) back to `None` when the model emits `null`, where this PR was returning the literal `"null"` string in all three parsers. #64518 is also authored by the issue reporter and landed the broader fix first.

This PR was a narrower subset of that work and carried the `null`-string regression, so there is no independent change left worth landing here. Dropping it in favor of #64518.

(You were also right that the branch had picked up the #61547 scheduler and model-runner commits; that is moot once this is closed.)

I reviewed the fix rather than treating this as a mechanical dedupe: #64518 keeps the raw model text for a string-typed parameter under those schema forms, resolves the admitted type across `$ref` unions, and has the `test_glimmer_keeps_decoding_optional_string` coverage for the optional-string case. Authored with AI assistance.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Thanks for working on this. I noticed #64518 fixes the same issue and was opened a little earlier by the issue author.

I ran both, and the difference I'd look at first is an `Optional[str]` parameter where the model writes `null`: this PR returns the string `"null"` in all three parsers, while main and #64518 return `None`. #64518 covers `enum`, `$ref` and `additionalProperties` string schemas too.

The branch seems to include the #61547 commits as well (scheduler, model runner), so you may want to drop those.
